expectations.evidence: References Biome, Vitest, Drizzle ORM, gramjs, pino, Zod, Claude API, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, ESLint for UI apps by name. Rules are deeply tailored to Backcom's pipeline architecture.
All rules are TypeScript/Node.js specific. No Python rules present.

Section 2 'Anti-patterns to reject' explicitly calls out: (a) toBeDefined() as only assertion, (b) tests that compute expected score same way rule-engine.ts does (implementation-mirroring), (c) snapshot tests for classifier output or scored leads, (d) vague test names with good/bad examples, (e) mocking the function under test. All 5 of 5 addressed.
Backcom output is 252 lines with 10 major sections. This is larger than the minimal project (119 lines, 8 sections), which is the correct proportional relationship.

Section 10 covers Telegram-specific rules (account safety, ban prevention, FloodWaitError, warm-up periods), forex compliance (no profit claims, NFA disclaimer, no broker names), rate limiting (per-group cooldown, per-hour/daily caps, jitter), and content safety rules.
Section 'Where should these rules live?' offers three options: A) Add to CLAUDE.md (recommended), B) Create separate docs/QUALITY.md, C) Both.

Opening summary states 'The existing CLAUDE.md is comprehensive (300+ lines)... The rules below focus on gaps not already covered.' Multiple sections begin with notes like '> CLAUDE.md already defines...' and a summary table at the end explicitly maps what is new vs existing.
